conventions.convention: The RN datum uses signature (−+++), f(r)=1−2M/r+(q_e²+q_m²)/r², and F=−q_e r⁻² dx⁰∧dr+q_m ω_S², with the sphere oriented outward. Coordinates x⁰,r and mass and charge parameters have length units.

Circular null geodesics are smooth, nonconstant, affinely parametrized equatorial geodesics with nonzero angular momentum. Instability means a growing solution of the radial linearization at fixed E and angular momentum; no wave-decay estimate is asserted. Countable Choice is explicitly adopted in Facts & Assumptions for the connection supplier.

Surface gravity is signed and normalized by the Killing field whose metric square tends to −1 at infinity: κ±=(r±−r∓)/(2r±²). The horizon supplier requires Q²>0 and makes only a local Killing-horizon claim.

The throat scaling fixes m>0 and q_e²+q_m²=m², takes dimensionless λ>0, and uses x⁰=T/λ and r=m+λR on R>0. Convergence is uniform for every coordinate derivative on compact subsets; neither convergence through R=0 nor uniform control of the original exterior is asserted.
The surface-gravity counterexample fixes the mass m and uses the electric sequence q_e,n=m√(1−n⁻²), q_m,n=0, indexed by integers n≥2. Every sequence member is strictly subextremal.

load_bearing.statement: For m>0 and 0≤Q²=q_e²+q_m²<m², the outer circular null radius is r_ph+=(3m+√(9m²−8Q²))/2. It lies strictly above r+=m+√(m²−Q²) and is a strict local maximum of h=f/r². At fixed E and nonzero angular momentum ℓ, the radial linearization is ρ̈−ν²ρ=0, where ν²=−ℓ²h″(r_ph+)/2>0, and has the growing mode exp(νs).

For m>0 and q_e²+q_m²=m², the pullbacks under Φλ(T,R,ω)=(T/λ,m+λR,ω) converge with every coordinate derivative uniformly on compact subsets of R×(0,∞)×S² to g₀=−R²m⁻²dT²+m²R⁻²dR²+m²γ_S² and F₀=−q_e m⁻²dT∧dR+q_m ω_S².
